newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen futures end higher on JGBs' jump.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen futures end higher on JGBs' jump.

text.p: Key September three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures ended Friday's TIFFE day session higher, following a sharp rise in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures.
The September contract settled at an intraday high of 99.33. The volume was 23,573 contracts.
The key March JGB futures contract closed up 0.56 at an intraday high of 126.22.

Some players sold Euroyen futures after the Bank of Japan (BOJ) said in its quarterly economic report that it was necessary to closely watch the effects of rising import prices, but selling was short-lived, traders said.

"The BOJ's announcement yesterday to postpone the release of quarterly "tankan" business survey gave rise to speculation that the BOJ was concerned about stock prices. Today's report seems to support such views," said a city bank trader.
The BOJ said in the report that it would closely watch the effect of recent falls in Japanese stock prices on corporate sentiment.
The BOJ said on Thursday it would release the tankan in early April instead of late February.
A BOJ official told reporters that the decision was aimed at boosting the accuracy of the survey and making its results easier to use.
However, some market players suspect that the BOJ may be wishing to avoid the negative impact the survey might have on stock prices before the fiscal year-end in March, traders said.
In the interbank money market, key unsecured overnight call money was traded at 0.47 percent, down from Thursday's weighted average of 0.49 percent.
The BOJ injected a net 600 billion yen into the money market on Friday morning, maintaining a neutral stance.
Key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) were offered at 0.53 percent. One-month and two-month CDs were offered at 0.51 percent. All CD rates were unchanged from Thursday.
"Some dealers may be keen to purchase three-month CDs at 0.54 percent. However, issuers are in no hurry to raise funds," said a trader at an investment trust firm.
